title: Does the Stock Market Stigmatize Banks that Borrow from the Fed? - Liberty Street Economics
gist: NY Fed Liberty Street Economics research on the March 2023 bank run finds that a bank's first Discount Window loan made stock investors more sensitive to its uninsured-deposit and capital weaknesses, while first BTFP borrowing drew no penalty. The authors attribute the gap to the BTFP's more generous terms (face-value collateral, lower rate) and lack of historical stigma, suggesting purpose-built crisis facilities work better.

themes.theme: Discount Window stigma in the 2023 bank run

insights.claim: NY Fed research finds that after a bank's first Discount Window (DW) borrowing during March 2023, stock investors became significantly more sensitive to that bank's uninsured-deposit and capital weaknesses within 4-7 trading days.
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: DW usage remains a negative equity signal for banks; expect stock penalties if a bank's DW draw becomes known.
insights.locator: The chart above shows the change

insights.claim: Banks that borrowed only from the Bank Term Funding Program (BTFP) in March 2023 saw no significant change in stock investors' risk perceptions, meaning investors did not penalize BTFP use.
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: Purpose-built crisis facilities can provide liquidity without triggering equity stigma.
insights.quote: Thus, investors did not penalize banks for using the BTFP.
insights.locator: For banks that used only the BTFP

insights.claim: Discount Window stigma can cause banks to resist Fed borrowing during panics, hampering the Fed's crisis response, and the problem is acute for publicly traded banks whose stock prices instantly reflect market views.
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: Lender-of-last-resort effectiveness depends on usage; stigma can turn liquidity stress into solvency runs.

insights.claim: Stigma around the Fed's Discount Window has persisted for decades, spiking in the 2007–08 financial crisis and resurfacing around the spring 2023 bank run, even though borrower identities are only disclosed after two years.
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: Anonymity does not eliminate stigma; markets infer DW usage regardless.
insights.locator: Borrowing from either facility is anonymous

insights.claim: The BTFP lent against the face value of Treasuries, agency debt and agency MBS for up to one year at typically lower rates, whereas the DW lent against market value, so choosing the worse DW terms signalled a bank had exhausted better options or needed to pledge illiquid loans.
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: Facility design (collateral valuation, rate) determines the information content of borrowing, and therefore stigma.
insights.quote: A bank willing to accept the worse deal may be one that had already exhausted better options
insights.locator: Why the Two Facilities Might Differ

insights.claim: The authors argue the BTFP's newness, lack of historical baggage and targeting at the specific March 2023 problem helped it avoid the stigma that has hardened around the Discount Window.
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: Expect future crises to be met with new, purpose-built Fed facilities rather than reliance on the DW.

insights.claim: Of the 48 banks that drew on the Discount Window during the study period, about half borrowed more than once and about a third of those returned repeatedly, showing DW borrowing was persistent.
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: Repeated DW use flags banks with sustained funding stress.

insights.claim: The NY Fed authors measure investor risk perceptions using bank-level stock 'betas' to portfolios isolating four weaknesses: uninsured deposits, unrealized securities losses, cash holdings and capital strength (CET1).
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: Factor betas to balance-sheet-risk portfolios offer a real-time market gauge of which bank vulnerabilities are being priced.
insights.locator: Measuring Investor Perceptions About Bank Risk

insights.claim: Bank-risk betas were statistically zero before the 2023 bank run but turned positive and rose sharply just before the run began on March 7, showing investors abruptly became sensitized to balance-sheet risk.
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: Bank risk pricing is regime-dependent: it can jump from zero to acute almost overnight.
insights.locator: The chart below shows that beta

insights.claim: The announcement of the BTFP on March 12, 2023 made investors less sensitized to the risks of banks most likely to benefit from it, per the authors' companion paper.
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: Credible policy backstops can compress bank-equity risk premia quickly.

insights.claim: Between March 8 and March 31, 2023, 34 sample banks made a first BTFP draw and 33 a first DW draw (10 used both), compared against 207 banks that used neither, over seven trading days around each first loan using a staggered event-timing method.
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: Small sample sizes mean conclusions about facility stigma should be held cautiously.

insights.claim: The authors caution that the head-to-head DW vs BTFP comparison is not statistically decisive and that they cannot fully separate the signal from borrowing from the reasons a bank needed to borrow.
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: Treat the stigma asymmetry as suggestive, not proof.
insights.quote: We caution that the head-to-head comparison between the two facilities is not statistically decisive.

insights.claim: The authors conclude that emergency programs designed for a specific crisis and free of historical burden are more likely to succeed as lender-of-last-resort tools than legacy facilities like the Discount Window.
insights.speaker: Natalia Fischl-Lanzoni
insights.so_what: Policy implication: in the next banking stress, watch for ad-hoc Fed facilities as the effective backstop.
insights.quote: emergency programs designed to address a specific crisis, and not carrying the burden of history, are more likely to be successful
